pr_body:
Added bt_rpmsg_close() implementation, any comments appreciated, addressing #52907 
In short, function invokes reset CMD on network core, cleans stuff related to IPC and puts network core in reset.
Checking for freed endpoints changed due to situation I observed: when network core creates two endpoints, the IPC on the app core has listed endpoints with names even if they are not bounded.

Fixes #52907
pr_comments:
Some thoughts:
- Some of this is very nrf53 specific. Is it possible to make it more generic? Not sure if anyone else is using this driver, but anyway.
- Sending HCI Reset is a good start. Some applications may want to do a full teardown of the Bluetooth subsystem. Maybe we should add a function `bt_disable_raw` and call that on the netcore when `bt_disable` is called on the app core? This would need some changes to the hci_rpmsg sample. It does also not have to be done in this PR.

I am not very familiar with the ipc stuff, mostly speaking from Bluetooth perspective.

I agree with @hermabe , could you put all the nrf53-specific functions in an `nrf53_support.c` file? it can be in the same dir, and you can use `target_sources_ifdef(` with the right nrf53 define to compile it.

@hermabe I don't get your second point, the PR will put the whole netcore in reset, so no need to teardown the bluetooth hci_raw driver (on the netcore). `bt_disable` already calls the `.close` method of the HCI driver.

> the PR will put the whole netcore in reset

Only on nrf53. But I see your point that this will also disable Bluetooth.

I guess there are multiple different "resets". HCI Reset, bt_disable and core reset. I think some applications will only want to disable bluetooth on the netcore and start using some other proprietary protocol. This might be too application specific for us to implement here.

>  `bt_disable` already calls the `.close` method of the HCI driver.

It only calls `.close` on the app core HCI rpmsg driver. The driver on the netcore does not get closed. `bt_enable_raw` calls `.open()`, which is why I thought we might want `bt_disable_raw` that calls `.close()`.

@jori-nordic nrf53 specific functions moved to external file, name of functions are not specific to HW so the implementations can be different based on build params. Last idea was to declare on/off functions as weak inside rpmsg.c (with no reset) and based on any config we can add external files with declarations with reset.
@carlocaione pinging to know if the vrings changes are fine

@jori-nordic For me, everything looks OK. On our side, we have put bodies of cpunet_forceon/off() functions inside the rpmsg driver. But it works the same way. Thank you for reopening.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Add functionality for bt_disable for off-chip HCI drivers
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
At the moment bt_disable cannot be used with rpmsg, spi, uart etc. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Currently bt_hci_driver.open just sets up communication for off-chip HCI drivers, this would also have to also set up the controller on this command. A bt_hci_driver.close functionality would have to be implemented that tears down the controller.
comments: In my project I have observed the same issue. Is there any update?
We're facing the same issue as well.

I was doing something like this in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/55648 .
The building blocks are here, it just needs implementation (has to be different for every driver).
